title: The 2020 COVID-19 lockdown made recorded UK spring butterfly flight dates about 16 days late, and this artifact can change temperature slopes and trends in 2005-2024 analyses
abstract: Question: the spring 2020 lockdown cut UK Butterfly Monitoring Scheme (UKBMS) transect walks by about 72% in April and early May, in a warm and very sunny spring. How large is the artifact in the public UKBMS phenology metrics, and does it change climate analyses that include 2020? Data: UKBMS phenology 2024 (1995-2024, 33 species, 585,557 site-species-years), UKBMS site indices, CRU TS 4.09 local temperature. Method: a plan written before the models; for each species and metric, site effects, a local temperature window and a linear time term fitted without one held-out year; 2020 compared with 19 other held-out years (2005-2024). Results: for 12 spring species the mean 2020 first-day anomaly was +16.4 days (other years -12.1 to +8.4); Peacock +35.8 and Brimstone +32.5 days. The anomaly decreased with the species' flight season (Spearman -0.82, 30 species). Summer species were early in 2020 (-5.1 days), as a warm spring predicts. The excess was larger in Scotland than in England (+16.6 days, 95% CI 8.4 to 24.3); Wales and Northern Ireland were uncertain. Only 30-37% of sites kept a 2020 site index for four spring single-brood species (usual 73-80%). 2021 was not an outlier. Consequences: 2020 changed 1995-2024 temperature slopes by about 5-7%, but post-hoc checks showed larger effects in short windows (Peacock first-day slope -1.9 to +0.3 days per C in 2010-2024), a spurious warm-end curvature for Brimstone, and +1.7 days per decade in 2005-2024 first-day trends of adult-hibernating species. About 50 campaign publications on UK butterfly timing include 2020. Limitations: no visit dates in the public data; simple expected-value model; few Welsh and Northern Irish records; post-hoc checks not planned; campaign publications were not rerun. Analyses should exclude 2020 for species that fly before July or show that results do not change.
